article_title: Usage of augmented reality (AR) and development of e-learning outcomes: An empirical evaluation of students’ e-learning experience
citation: Baabdullah, Alsulaimani, Allamnakhrah, Alalwan, Dwivedi & Rana. (2021). Usage of Augmented Reality (AR) and Development of e-Learning Outcomes: An Empirical Evaluation of Students' e-Learning Experience. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Usage+of+Augmented+Reality+AR+and+Development+of+e-Learning+Outcomes+An+Empirical+Evaluation+of+Students+e-Learning+Experience
title: UGT-based conceptual model of students' e-learning experience with augmented reality learning applications
description: The article adapts Uses and Gratifications Theory (Katz et al., 1974) into a conceptual model in which four UGT benefit dimensions — "personal integrative benefits (PIB); cognitive benefits (CGB); social integrative benefits (SIB); and affective benefits (AB)" — act as antecedents of students' e-learning experience with AR learning applications, which in turn drives e-learning performance. The model extends UGT with telepresence as an additional antecedent and technostress as a moderator of all four benefit-experience paths. It was operationalised as a two-stage SEM model with 34 scale items across eight latent constructs and tested on 325 valid survey responses.
requirements: Respondents must be actively engaged in using AR learning applications for the experience constructs to be meaningful
constraints: Tested with undergraduate students at four large Saudi universities in science, computer science, engineering and medicine disciplines; the article does not claim generalisation beyond this context
target_learning_goals: positive e-learning experience with augmented reality learning applications
examples: The model was validated via a questionnaire survey of 500 approached undergraduates (325 valid, 65% response rate) using seven-point Likert scales, with measurement and structural model fit indices reported
key_sources: Baabdullah, Alsulaimani, Allamnakhrah, Alalwan, Dwivedi & Rana. (2021). Usage of Augmented Reality (AR) and Development of e-Learning Outcomes: An Empirical Evaluation of Students' e-Learning Experience. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Usage+of+Augmented+Reality+AR+and+Development+of+e-Learning+Outcomes+An+Empirical+Evaluation+of+Students+e-Learning+Experience

article_title: Thoracic ultrasound competence for ultrasound-guided pleural procedures.
citation: McCracken DJ, Laursen CB, Barker G, Gleeson FV, Cullen KM, Rahman NM. (2019). Thoracic ultrasound competence for ultrasound-guided pleural procedures. European Respiratory Review. https://doi.org/10.1183/16000617.0090-2019
title: UG-STAT (ultrasound-guided thoracentesis skills and tasks assessment test)
description: UG-STAT is the formative and summative assessment tool used throughout the Australasian TUS competence pathway. It "assesses 100 points over 11 domains related to the British Thoracic Society guidelines", covering basic ultrasound parameters, recognition of common pleural effusion appearances, performing TUS on a model or mannequin, and marking an appropriate site for pleural drainage. The review states it has been validated to discriminate between novice, intermediate and advanced users, and it is used for formative assessments after 5–10 and 20 scans and the barrier assessment after 40 scans.
requirements: Administered by trained assessors within the Thoracic Society of Australia and New Zealand pathway, with a minimum pass mark of 90% for competence recognition
constraints: The validated pass mark corresponds with advanced practice and fails to recognise gradations of competence between basic and advanced practitioners
target_learning_goals: thoracic ultrasound skill and pleural effusion site marking
examples: The Australian pathway uses UG-STAT for two formative assessments (after 5–10 and 20 scans) and a barrier assessment after 40 scans by an independent assessor
key_sources: McCracken DJ, Laursen CB, Barker G, Gleeson FV, Cullen KM, Rahman NM. (2019). Thoracic ultrasound competence for ultrasound-guided pleural procedures. European Respiratory Review. https://doi.org/10.1183/16000617.0090-2019

article_title: Simulation-based ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia curriculum for anesthesiology residents.
citation: Kim T. Edward, Tsui Ban C.H. (2019). Simulation-based ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia curriculum for anesthesiology residents. Korean J Anesthesiol. https://doi.org/10.4097/kja.d.18.00317
title: UGRA performance requires a triad of interrelated skills: image acquisition, anatomical interpretation, and hand-eye coordination
description: The article frames successful ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia as resting on three distinct but interrelated skills. It states that "a triad of three distinct but interrelated skills are required: image acquisition, anatomical interpretation, and hand-eye coordination (Fig. 1)", describing a dynamic process of needle guidance with simultaneous transducer adjustment. This triad organizes the review's curriculum recommendations, with simulation modalities mapped to each skill component.
requirements: In-depth knowledge of anatomy is described as a prerequisite before learners can progress into advanced sonoanatomy rather than pattern recognition
constraints: The framework is specific to ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia procedures
examples: Fig. 1 depicts the skills required for ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia
key_sources: Kim T. Edward, Tsui Ban C.H. (2019). Simulation-based ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia curriculum for anesthesiology residents. Korean J Anesthesiol. https://doi.org/10.4097/kja.d.18.00317
